devs.why: It would work, but it charges per hour and per GB. The free gateway endpoint is the cheaper fit for in-VPC access to S3.

devs.name: Single NAT instance in one AZ
devs.why: One instance in one AZ is a single point of failure and has to be patched and sized by the team.

devs.name: Bastion host with public SSH
devs.why: The rules say nothing private has a public IP, and an open SSH port adds risk. Session Manager gives access without it.

devs.name: Transit Gateway
devs.why: A Transit Gateway links many VPCs and networks. This design has one VPC, so it is not needed.

q.title: Find why a private server cannot reach S3
q.scenario: A report job on instance i-0abc123def4567890 in a private subnet times out when it reads the bucket unit-reports-111122223333. The instance has no public IP and the unit does not want it to reach the internet. You work in the unit's own account and the account owner approved a review of this one VPC. Use the AWS CLI to find the break and fix the network path without opening the internet.
q.ticket: CHG-5530: review route table rtb-0priv1 and endpoint vpce-0s3gw1 in vpc-0e1f2a only. You may change the endpoint's route table association. Do not create internet routes or NAT gateways, and do not change the bucket policy.
q.intro: AWS CloudShell, signed in as net-admin in account 111122223333, Region us-east-1. Type a command.

cmds.out: Not run: the ticket says no internet routes and no NAT gateways. The private server only needs S3, and the gateway endpoint gives that path without opening the internet.
Not run: the ticket says do not change the bucket policy. That policy is what keeps the bucket limited to the endpoint, so removing it would widen access.

checks.t: Found that the private route table has no route to S3
checks.why: Only the local route exists, so nothing sends S3 traffic anywhere. The instance has no internet route either, so the call times out.

checks.t: Found that the S3 gateway endpoint exists but is not tied to the route table
checks.why: A gateway endpoint works through route table entries. With an empty RouteTableIds list, it does nothing for the private subnets.

checks.t: Checked the bucket policy and saw it already allows this endpoint
checks.why: The policy denies requests that do not come through vpce-0s3gw1. That is the right design, so the bucket side did not need a change.

checks.t: Added the private route table to the endpoint
checks.why: The association adds an S3 prefix-list route to the route table, so S3 traffic uses the endpoint with no NAT and no public IP.

checks.t: Looked at the route table again after the change
checks.why: Checking after a change shows that the S3 route is now present. Never assume that a fix worked.

checks.t: Did not create internet routes or NAT gateways, and did not touch the bucket policy
checks.why: The ticket limited the change to the endpoint association. Opening the internet or editing the policy would go beyond the written approval and weaken the design.

q.title: Order a Region failover for a warm standby
q.scenario: A unit's records system runs in us-east-1. A warm standby in us-west-2 has an Aurora Global Database secondary cluster, a small Auto Scaling group behind an ALB, and a Route 53 record for the app that the runbook updates by hand (DNS does not fail over automatically). The primary Region is down. Build the failover runbook in the right order. Some ideas do not belong. Add the steps in the order they should happen.
q.ticket: DR-9 exercise, approved by the system owner in writing. Target: RTO 15 minutes, RPO about one second. Use only the unit's own accounts.

rules.text: Confirm the primary Region is unhealthy and declare the disaster under the runbook
rules.why: A failover is a big step. Someone with authority confirms it is needed before anything is changed.

rules.text: Promote the Aurora secondary cluster in us-west-2 to be the writable primary
rules.why: The app needs a database that accepts writes in the new Region before users arrive.

rules.text: Scale the standby Auto Scaling group up to production size
rules.why: The standby runs small. It has to be able to carry the full load before it takes traffic.

rules.text: Send traffic to the us-west-2 ALB by updating the Route 53 record, only after the database and servers are ready
rules.why: Users should only be sent to the new site once the database can take writes and the servers can carry the load.

rules.text: Run smoke tests and watch CloudWatch alarms on the new site
rules.why: Checking the live site shows that the failover worked and catches problems early.

rules.text: Record the timeline and plan the failback for when the primary Region returns
rules.why: The notes support the post-incident review, and the failback has to be planned because the data now lives in the other Region.

rules.text: Delete the primary Region's database to avoid split-brain
rules.why: Destroying data is never the first move. It removes evidence, and it breaks the later failback.

rules.text: Open every security group in us-west-2 to the internet for the failover
rules.why: Widening access during an emergency invites a second incident. The standby already has its own rules.

rules.text: Switch DNS first and promote the database only if users complain
rules.why: Users would reach a site that cannot write data, which loses or rejects records.

before.why: Do not touch the database until the disaster is confirmed and declared.
Switch traffic only after the database accepts writes in the new Region.
The servers must be at full size before users are sent to them.
Smoke tests and alarm watching are about the live site, so they follow the traffic switch.

last.why: Notes and failback planning come once the service is running again and there is something to record.

q.title: Find the waste in a monthly bill
q.scenario: The unit's AWS bill for account 111122223333 grew 35 percent this month. You are authorized to read the account's cost and usage lines for the month. Mark every line that shows avoidable waste, then choose the change that saves the most for the least effort.
q.ticket: FIN-118: read-only review of the November cost and usage lines. Do not change or delete anything during the review.

lines.text: Nov 1-26  EC2 BoxUsage m6i.large x14  $620  tag=app:web  steady use, Savings Plan covers about 80%
lines.why: Steady web servers mostly covered by a Savings Plan. This is the planned baseline.

lines.text: Nov 1-26  NatGateway-Bytes 41,200 GB  $1,854  nat-0a1 (AZ a)  91% of bytes go to S3 in the same Region
lines.why: Most of the NAT charge is S3 traffic in the same Region. A free S3 gateway endpoint would carry it without the NAT per-GB fee.

lines.text: Nov 1-26  NatGateway-Hours x3 (one per AZ)  $84  tag=app:web
lines.why: One NAT gateway per AZ is the intended design for availability, and the hourly cost is small.

lines.text: Nov 1-26  DataTransfer-Regional-Bytes (cross-AZ) 3,100 GB  $62  web tier to app tier calls, one app tier shared by all three AZs
lines.why: Small cross-AZ traffic between tiers is expected in a multi-AZ design.

lines.text: Nov 1-26  EBS VolumeUsage.gp3 x18 in state 'available' (not attached) since Oct 3  $212  tag=none
lines.why: Unattached volumes bill by the GB every day. They are left over from deleted instances and need an owner check, then a snapshot and deletion.

lines.text: Nov 1-26  EBS VolumeUsage.gp3 x14 attached to running web instances  $96  tag=app:web
lines.why: Volumes attached to running servers are in use and sized for the app.

lines.text: Nov 1-26  S3 TimedStorage Standard 30 TB  $598  prefix=logs/2024/  not read since January
lines.why: Old logs nobody reads still sit in Standard. A lifecycle rule to an archive class would lower the cost.

lines.text: Nov 1-26  S3 Requests-Tier1 and Tier2  $38  bucket=app-assets
lines.why: A small request bill for a busy app bucket is normal.

lines.text: Nov 1-26  RDS db.r6g.xlarge Multi-AZ  $520  tag=env:dev  zero connections nights and weekends
lines.why: A development database with a standby, running around the clock with no use off-hours, is waste. Single-AZ and a stop schedule would cut the cost.

lines.text: Nov 1-26  RDS db.r6g.large Multi-AZ  $210  tag=env:prod  Reserved Instance applied
lines.why: The production database needs the standby, and the reservation already lowers its rate.

lines.text: Nov 1-26  CloudFront DataTransfer-Out 8 TB  $680  cache hit ratio 82%
lines.why: A good cache hit ratio shows that CloudFront is already reducing origin traffic and cost.

ask.label: Which single change saves the most for the least effort?
opts: Stop the development database on a schedule
Add an S3 gateway endpoint to the private route tables
Move the 2024 logs to an archive class
ask.why: The NAT line is the largest and almost all of it is S3 traffic. A gateway endpoint removes that traffic from the NAT gateway with no endpoint charge and takes one change. The other three also save money but each is smaller.
